title: Social learning theory
examples: How is watching someone else do something different from just being told to do it?
What is the difference between learning by experience and learning by observation?
Can you give an example of self-efficacy in action?

explain.say: Today we are exploring social learning theory. This theory suggests we learn from observing others. We do not just learn from direct experience alone.

draw.text: Social Learning Theory: Learning by Observation

explain.say: Albert Bandura is a key figure in this area. He proposed that learning is much more complex than simple conditioning. We learn through observing models.
Modeling involves paying attention to the behavior shown. We watch the model and pay close attention to the details. This attention is the first step.

items: Reproduction: Being able to copy the action

draw.text: Modeling: Attention is the first step

explain.say: Next, we must remember what we observe. This is called retention. We encode the behavior into our memory for later use. We must be able to recall the steps.
The third step is reproduction. This means we must physically be able to perform the action. Practice is necessary to turn memory into skill. This requires physical ability.
A real-life example is watching a skilled athlete. You observe their technique for a jump. You remember the steps and practice until you can perform it yourself.

draw.text: Real Life: Learning a new sport skill

faq.q: Does social learning theory mean we learn everything just by watching?
faq.a: No, it means observation is a very powerful way to learn. We still need some personal experience and motivation to act on what we see.
asks: Is observation the only way to learn?
Do we need experience to learn from others?

faq.q: What is self-efficacy and why is it important?
faq.a: Self-efficacy is your belief in your own ability to succeed at a task. High self-efficacy makes you more likely to try difficult things.

faq.q: Is modeling the same as direct instruction?
faq.a: No, direct instruction is being told exactly what to do. Modeling is learning by seeing someone else do it first. It is a different process.
asks: Is watching the same as being taught?
What is the difference between telling and showing?

faq.q: Can I learn something I see if I am scared to try it?
faq.a: Yes, you can learn the steps just by watching and remembering. However, your motivation and belief in yourself help you actually perform the skill.
asks: Does fear stop learning from models?
Why is motivation important in this theory?

faq.q: What is the role of attention in this theory?
faq.a: Attention is crucial because if you do not pay attention to the model, you cannot encode the behavior into your memory. You must watch carefully.
asks: Why must I pay attention to the model?
What happens if I ignore what I see?

facts: Social learning theory emphasizes that learning occurs in a social context.
Bandura highlighted that self-efficacy is a major determinant of behavior.
The process of modeling involves attention, retention, reproduction, and motivation.
Learning can occur without direct reinforcement from the environment.

quiz.say: A student watches an older sibling successfully solve a complex maths problem.

options.show: The student is using observational learning.
options.say: The student is using observational learning.

quiz.why: This is a classic example of modeling, where learning occurs by watching a model.

wrong.0: The theory suggests learning can happen without explicit teaching.
wrong.1: Motivation is the final step; the initial learning requires observation first.
wrong.3: Practice is the reproduction stage, but the initial learning came from watching.

quiz.say: If you believe you cannot pass an exam, even if you study, what concept is low?
quiz.why: Self-efficacy is specifically defined as one's belief in their own capabilities to perform a task.

wrong.1: Motivation is the desire to act, while self-efficacy is the belief in the ability to act.
wrong.2: Attention is a process of focus, not a measure of belief in ability.
wrong.3: Retention refers to remembering the information, not the confidence level.

quiz.say: Which stage requires the physical ability to perform the learned skill?
quiz.why: Reproduction is the stage where the stored memory is converted into actual, physical performance.

wrong.1: Attention is the initial mental focus on the model's actions.
wrong.2: Retention is the mental act of storing the observed information in memory.
wrong.3: Motivation is the emotional drive to perform the skill, not the physical act itself.
